OBSERVATIONS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS
1 - Observation: Valid food managers certification is required and was not available upon request at the point of inspection. Facility or PIC must ensure at least one individual within the facility must acquire a valid food managers certification within 60 days of their employment. Also, individuals designated to obtain the food handlers certification are required to obtain the certification within 30 days of their employment. All certifications must be made available upon request at the time of inspection.  
Code Section: 113947.1 
Correct By: 04/02/2024
5 - Observation: Observed tomatoes, onions, mushrooms, and bell peppers being potentially contaminated due to employee directly touching the food items without properly washing hands. Product voluntarily condemned and destroyed due to this occurrence. Discard contaminated food products immediately and employees shall not commit any act that may result in the contamination or adulteration of food. Employees shall appropriately and thoroughly wash hands and wear gloves when necessary.  
Code Section: 113953.3 
Corrective Action: Employees shall appropriately and throughly wash hands and wear gloves when necessary. 
6 - Observation: Observed primary handwashing facility inaccessible due to cooking utensils that had been placed within it. Handwashing sinks must be unobstructed and used for the sole purpose of handwashing. 
Code Section: 113953.1 
6 - Observation: Observe a primary handwashing sink without single use paper towels available within the designated dispenser. All hand wash sinks continuously provide hot and cold running water under pressure, single use soap, and paper towels in dispensers. 
Code Section: 113953.2 
Corrective Action: Provide hot and cold running water under pressure, single use soap and paper towels in dispensers. 
14 - Observation: Observed a cutting board with notable indentations and stains. Remove/replace cuttings boards that show noticeable signs of wear and tear due to the potential chance of bacteria forming on the surface of the cutting board. Also, routinely clean and sanitize food contact surfaces and utensils after becoming contaminated or at least once every 4 hours; handle and store equipment to prevent contamination.  
Code Section: 114113 
Correct By: 04/02/2024
23 - Observation: Observed multiple dead flies that has been accumulated on a fly trap directly above a food prep surface within the employee only area of the facility. Facility must maintain the facility to prevent the entrance and/or harborage of animals, birds, and vermin; obtain professional services as needed. Facility must immediately remove any/all signs of infestation and thoroughly clean/sanitize all contaminated areas. Maintain food to prevent the harborage of rodents. Contact a pest operator. Major infestation subject to closure. 
Code Section: 114259.1 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
23 - Observation: Observed significant accumulation of rodent droppings located within the employee kitchen area of the facility. Facility had an accumulation of rodent droppings surrounding soiled clothing and boxes located next to the kitchen exiting door. Once indicated to the PIC, PIC was instructed to immediately close the employee kitchen area and cease all food service in order to conduct a deep cleaning. Also, to completely sanitize the entire area in order to ensure contamination of surfaces and products is eliminated. Entry points allowing access into the employee kitchen area of the facility must be assessed and facility needs to adequately enclose problematic areas to prevent continuous vermin entry. Facility must remove all evidence of rodent infestation, clean, and sanitize all contaminated areas. Obtain professional pest control operator's exclusionary service agreement/report. Exclusionary service agreement/report must be provided to enforcement agency and should include a detailed list all areas that need to be addressed to exclude vermin. Complete all recommended vermin exclusion measures. 
Code Section: 114259.1 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
27 - Observation: Observed multiple containers within the reach-in and walk-in refrigeration units without any covering/lid. PIC must ensure covers are utilized to protect varying food items or adequately segregate food products to prevent contamination/cross-contamination of food. This requirements extends to ice intended for consumption. 
Code Section: 113986 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
Corrective Action: Cover and/or segregate food products to prevent contamination/cross-contamination of food. 
30 - Observation: Observed varying food ingredients/items stored in repurposed containers within the employee kitchen area of the facility without proper labeling. Once manufacturer packaging is removed or food items/ingredients are transferred to individual food-grade containers intended for storage, all food items must be properly labelled. Food items must be labeled in a manner that is easily viewable and legible for identification purposes  
Code Section: 114051 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
33 - Observation: Observed dust accumulation on the blower fan covers inside the walk-in refrigeration unit. Maintain an environment free of dust and debris. Clean nonfood-contact surface and maintain in sanitary condition. 
Code Section: 114115(c) 
Correct By: 04/02/2024
Corrective Action: Clean nonfood-contact surface and maintain in sanitary condition. 
33 - Observation: Observed grease residue accumulation on the ventilation system/hood within the employee kitchen area of the facility. Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment shall always be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Routinely clean nonfood-contact surface and maintain in sanitary condition. 
Code Section: 114115(c) 
Correct By: 04/02/2024
Corrective Action: Clean nonfood-contact surface and maintain in sanitary condition. 
35 - Observation: Observed a handwashing sink missing caulking and not permanently/securely fixed to the wall. PIC/facility is instructed to maintain all equipment and utensils clean, fully operational and in good repair. Remove malfunctioning equipment from facility. Obtain approval for all replacement equipment. 
Code Section: 114175 
Correct By: 04/26/2024
35 - Observation: Observed damaged/malfunctioning warewashing sink located in the employee kitchen area of the facility. Observed a leak stemming from a pipe associated with the warewashing unit. Once indicated to the PIC, PIC was instructed to contact a service provider to rectify the issue. Maintain all equipment and utensils clean, fully operational and in good repair. 
Code Section: 114175 
Correct By: 04/26/2024
35 - Observation: Observed debris accumulation inside the counter height reach-in refrigeration unit. Once indicated to the PIC, PIC was instructed to internally and externally clean the unit in order to ensure the items housed within the unit are kept in a sanitary environment. Maintain an environment free of dust and debris. Clean nonfood-contact surface and maintain in sanitary condition. 
Code Section: 114175 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
35 - Observation: Observed fryer with significant accumulation of grease on the side of the unit. PIC was instructed to continuously maintain all equipment and utensils clean, fully operational and in good repair. Maintain all equipment and utensils clean, fully operational and in good repair. Remove malfunctioning equipment from facility. Obtain approval for all replacement equipment 
Code Section: 114175 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
35 - Observation: Observed yellow substance on a baking sheet within walk-in refrigeration unit. Baking sheet/utensil was being used as a surface to store additional food items on. Once indicated to the PIC, PIC was instructed to internally clean the entire unit in order to ensure the items housed within the unit are kept in a sanitary environment. Maintain an environment free of dust and debris. Clean nonfood-contact surface and maintain in sanitary condition. 
Code Section: 114175 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
38 - Observation: Observed a light fixture above a food prep area within the employee back room with a covering/shatterproof shields completely off. A service/maintenance provider will need to be contacted in order to rectify the missing light fixture and prevent any contamination brought upon by exposed lighting. Provide adequate lighting in food preparation and dishwash areas; provide shatterproof shields for lights over food preparation areas, open food storage areas and dishwash areas.  
Code Section: 114252.1 
Correct By: 03/26/2024
39 - Observation: At time of inspection, no appropriate temperature measuring device was available for the sole purpose of adequate internal food temperature monitoring. Provide a thermometer accurate to /- 2?F in each refrigeration unit; maintain an approved metal probe thermometer onsite suitable for measuring food temperatures. 
Code Section: 114157 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
Corrective Action: Provide a thermometer accurate to +/- 2°F in each refrigeration unit; maintain an approved metal probe thermometer onsite suitable for measuring food temperatures. 
40 - Observation: Observed multiple multi-use wiping cloths in several preparation areas. Multi-use wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizing solution, such as a Chlorine solution at 100 ppm or Quaternary solution at 200 ppm. 
Code Section: 114185.1 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
44 - Observation: Observed the bottom of the exiting door with nonvector-proof condition within the back employee kitchen area of the facility. Exiting door sweep needs to be fixed or install a viable means to prevent the potential entering of vermin/insects from harboring within the facility. PIC was instructed to install a door sweep or other method to ensure employee kitchen area is fully enclosed. Maintain the facility to prevent the entrance and/or harborage of animals, birds, and vermin. 
Code Section: 114067 (j) 
Correct By: 04/26/2024
45 - Observation: Observed significant accumulation of grease underneath and behind the heat generating/cooking equipment. Maintain and clean floors, walls and ceilings in food preparation, food storage, utensil wash, restroom, and food service area(s). Improve cleaning in overlooked areas.  
Code Section: 114268.1 
Correct By: 03/29/2024
Corrective Action: Maintain and clean floors, walls and ceilings in food preparation, food storage, utensil wash, restroom, and food service area(s). 
Additional Comments:   PIC will be responsible for implementing any corrective measures indicated on fixed food facility inspection report. Permit to operate is suspended due to an imminent health hazard caused by a rodent infestation. Facility is instructed to close employee kitchen area until a cleaning and sanitization process is conducted. All potential entry points for vermin must be sealed. Employee kitchen area must remain closed to the public until given written notice following an follow-up inspection by this Division. Please contact this Division when the above has been corrected and the facility is ready for an inspection.

This is a NOTICE TO COMPLY. The required corrective action is described above. The governing laws are the California Health and Safety Code, Division 104, Part 7, RETAIL FOOD Chapters 1-13, otherwise known as the California Retail Food Code (Cal Code). The Napa County Department of Planning, Building, & Environmental Services may re-inspect the facility at any time to verify compliance with this Notice to Comply. Disputes to this inspection report must be made in writing within five (5) days of the signature date. Until such time as a decision is made regarding such a dispute, the contents of this report and the grade shall remain in effect. Please note that the Department uses a point system to grade facilities based on the number of points lost. 1-10 points deducted equals A; 11-20 points deducted equals B; 21-30 points equals C; greater than 30 points deducted equals a failed score (F), which necessitates immediate action and subjects the facility to additional inspections and/or legal actions to ensure the protection of the public health and safety. Facilities receiving two consecutive scores greater than 20 are subject to a re-inspection fee.

Major violations are those with a point value of 6 and minor violations are those with a point value of 2 or less. If, upon review by the Department, any errors are found that result in fewer points being deducted, the Department will make the correction and provide a copy of the corrected report to the facility owner/operator. The inspection report will be posted to the Internet no sooner than one County business day after the inspection is completed.

Facility Closed

As a result of violation(s) noted on this day and/or conditions that exist that pose an immediate danger to public health and safety, your permit is hereby suspended and you are being directed to close as per Section 114409 of Cal Code. You have the right to request a hearing in writing to show cause as to why your permit should be reinstated. Failure to request a hearing within fifteen (15) calendar days shall be deemed a waiver of the right to such hearing. This facility cannot be open for business until the permit is reinstated by this office of a new permit is applied for and obtained by the facility operator.
